text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russia's July 10 newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Unified Energy Systems is planning to float bonds totalling about five trillion roubles, said First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov.
- Russian investment bank ICFI, a unit of the Uneximbank-MFK financial group, and investment bank Renaissance Capital are merging to form a new investment bank with total assets of over $2 billion.
- Russia will pay off at least 4,2 trillion roubles as wages arrears to the military by the end of the year.
- While the Russian space crew fights problems at the troubled Mir station, mission control officials are keeping them in the dark about their families, the paper says.
- The government is planning to bring forward the launch in Russia of the world system of urgent communication during sea accidents.
- A new concept for developing Russian aviation is under consideration by the government, says Yevgeny Shaposhnikov, the president's aide on aviation.
- Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree scrapping quotas for government-sponsored exports of crude oil under so-called federal programmes.
- Russia has set a deadline for paying off massive wage arrears to the military and public sector workers.
- NATO has opened its doors in order to be closer to Russia's frontiers, says the paper, commenting on the results of the NATO summit in Madrid.

- The head of the investment bank Renaissance Capital, Boris Yordan, is likely to become head of the new super investment bank set up after the merger of Renaissance Capital with ICFI investment bank, says the paper.
